# Program status: the research tech tree {#sec-program-status}

This appendix is the one place in the book that is a live status ledger rather than a presentation of settled knowledge: it records which experiments are running, planned, done or stopped, with dates, so that a reader can see what is still open. Every row links to the dated lab-notebook entry (@sec-notebook) holding the preregistration and verdict. Polished chapters cite results only once they are in the DONE state here.

## The tech tree {#sec-tech-tree}

The program is run as an explicit tech tree: every experiment is a node
with a preregistered question, a dependency, an acceptance criterion, and a
dated verdict in the lab notebook (@sec-notebook). Two architectures recur
throughout. **ISLA** is the program's product: an SE(3)-equivariant
slice-routing surrogate, exact under rotations and translations by
construction, with an optional measure-weighted similarity gauge
(measure-weighted centroid and RMS-radius reference length) that is the
reference configuration for new runs since 2026-09-03; the checkpoints most
of this book reports predate that gauge and saw absolute scale through a
constant reference length (@sec-mt2-architecture). **GeoTransolver** is
the strongest baseline tested under this protocol, a soft-slice global-attention architecture
with pointwise raw-coordinate features and no equivariance contract; plain
**Transolver**, the same attention family without GeoTransolver's geometry
encoder, is the same-family control. The exact-kernel MeshTransformer, an
earlier design of this program, appears in the tree's history (nodes G3,
G3K, K0, V0) and nowhere in the recommendation. The central open question
the tree is now organized around is **whether ISLA has any accuracy
advantage once every model receives the freestream at the same unit scale,
and what its contracts are worth**: the unit-drive control (UDRV) showed
that the baselines' small-data deficit on HiLiftAeroML was an input-scaling
artifact of the comparison protocol, the unit-drive ladder (UDRV-L) and the
interior control (UDRV-INT) re-measure every remaining comparison, and the
book's verdict (@sec-verdict) is rewritten from their readouts.

This paragraph summarizes the ledger below as of 2026-09-09. The book's
headline is overturned by its own preregistered control. Every HiLiftAeroML
comparison fed GeoTransolver and Transolver the physical freestream velocity
(2,679.5 in/s) while ISLA received the unit direction; retrained with the
unit direction and nothing else changed (UDRV, done at 35 cases),
GeoTransolver scores 0.124 (0.111 at its better rate) and Transolver 0.115
against 0.381 and 0.404 with the physical velocity and ISLA's 0.138 (0.123
in the weights-off ablation), so both baselines are 1.1–1.25x more accurate
than ISLA (lower on 130 and 152 of 180 cases; 84 and 102 of
118 geometries), and each improved on 180 of 180 cases against its own
physical-drive lane (median 3.4x and 3.8x). The preregistered bars for
"the input scale carries a material part of the deficit" were 0.27 and
0.29; both arms passed far beyond them. The 2.8x at 35 cases, the 180/180
case wins, the 6x data-multiplier reading, the force-coefficient margin
(3% against 8–17%) and every steel-man control at 35 cases (CTRL, T1, INV,
A35, A35B) were measured against mis-scaled baselines; they remain
measurements of the physical-drive protocol and are no longer comparisons
of architectures. The 2.2x at 210 cases, the 1.8x and
1.4x on unseen geometries (W2-F) and the 5.0x at a fixed angle (W2) were
physical-drive measurements, and the unit-drive ladder has now read out at
every rung but 1,260 cases: GeoTransolver 0.83x of ISLA at 210 cases
(Transolver 0.91x), 0.76x at 4 geometries, 0.92x at 21, 0.78x at the fixed
angle (UDRV-L; the parity at 1,260 awaits its rerun,
running: GeoTransolver and Transolver at 210 cases, GeoTransolver at 4 and
21 training geometries, GeoTransolver at 1,260 cases queued behind budget;
the fixed-angle unit-drive lanes of UDRV are still training); its
preregistered prediction is that the baselines match or beat ISLA at every
rung, and ISLA has an advantage at a rung only if baseline ÷ ISLA ≥ 1.10
with ISLA lower on two thirds of the cases. On DrivAerML GeoTransolver's
surface lanes also consumed the physical velocity (38.9 m/s) and lead ISLA
1.2–1.3x at every training-set size regardless, so that lead is a lower
bound; GeoTransolver-volume consumes the same vector, and the interior
comparison (ISLA query tokens + SDF ahead on velocity 0.75x and behind on
pressure 1.08x and eddy viscosity 1.27x in float32, three seeds, at or above the training query
count) stands pending its unit-drive control (UDRV-INT). What no unit-drive
rerun can remove is ISLA's contracts: exact SE(3) covariance without a
frame estimate or a freestream at inference, a query-independent passive
decode (3.1x on the interior in float32, 3.0–3.7x on the surface), sampling-density
robustness with the similarity gauge, and the current code's 1.6 GiB
footprint at 3.7x GeoTransolver's step time (MEM-INST). ISLA-internal
results stand as measurements of ISLA: five single-factor ablations move
its 35-case error by at most 16%; its error responds to the number of
training geometries; its residual concentrates in the gap regions (HLREG).
On the sealed regime-extrapolation test both architectures degrade about
10x and the raw-coordinate discriminator was falsified. Every mechanism
candidate for the earlier cross-family transfer gap was resolved against
(locality, absolute scale, measure completeness, label noise) and the
exact-kernel line is closed on separated 3D aerodynamics. The independent
audit (@sec-nb-audit-2026-09-08) that raised the input-scale question also
found that the query-token configuration's prediction depends on query
count (repair committed; the interior advantage holds at or above the
training count; QMASS, done), that every ISLA interior arm received about
365 surface cells rather than 10,000, and that the rerun with 10,000 changes nothing (V0-SURF10K, null: 0.0572 / 0.0848 / 0.1187 against 0.0567 / 0.0853 / 0.1215), that no
HiLiftAeroML geometry is unexposed at the program level (EXPO, done), that
the geometry is the independent unit of the unseen-geometry statistics
(GEOSTAT, done), that the force errors are against sampled-cell label
integrals (FORCE-REF, ready), that the passive-decode price needs a
fixed-depth control (PASSIVE2, done via the companion's D1: passive route closed, 1.43x / 2.41x), and that the first-moment
representation limitation is removable by a cheap channel (MOM2, done;
MOM2-T done: the channel is free on DrivAerML surface pressure, 0.0583
against 0.0577); independent baselines outside the Transolver family are
queued behind UDRV-L (ABUPT).
Measured since: the fixed-angle unit-drive lanes (baselines ahead, 18 of 18
geometries), the 4-geometry unit-drive rung (baselines ahead by the mean,
even by geometry), the interior unit-drive control (null: the interior
ordering stands), the width control and the 10,000-cell rerun (both null
for the eddy-viscosity gap), the interior density and neighbour channels
(both null, QTDENS), the measure-weight tests (weights cost 12% at 35 cases
under either metric, 17% at 4 geometries, 10.6% at the fixed angle; 2.9% on
DrivAerML), the float32 re-evaluation of every checkpoint (FP32-EVAL), the
fast softmax kernel's neutrality (KERNEL), the 35-case draw intervals
(CAMPA: between-draw spread 3–11x the seed spread), and the companion's
pose benchmark (ISLA 6–19% ahead of augmented baselines in arbitrary
poses), few-shot transfer (GeoTransolver 31%, ISLA 6%) and diversity trade.
Still running: the remaining UDRV-L rungs (210 and 21 geometries near
completion; 1,260, 510, deflection and 20k tokens I/O-throttled), the
weights-off ladder's last three rungs, the 210-case draw campaign, the
scaling study's baselines at 512 × 80k cells, and the companion's
conditioning (T1), rung/mixing split and width-matched interior pair.

## Provenance {#sec-provenance}

Every quantitative claim in the polished chapters is computed live from a
checked-in artifact under `examples/cfd/mesh_transformer/results/` (JSON
reductions of evaluation runs, each named with the date of the run that
produced it), or is a literal quoted from one of those files with the file
named in the caption. The lab notebook (@sec-notebook) holds, for every
artifact, the preregistration that preceded the run, the launch record,
and the verdict entry; the tech-tree ledger above links each node to those
entries. Training runs, checkpoints and per-point predictions live on the
cluster in the task directory named in the notebook and are not needed to
regenerate any figure in this book.

Two protocol facts a reader should carry into every chapter: all HiLift and
DrivAerML training runs used the same frozen recipe (10,000 sampled surface
points per case, 500 epochs, bfloat16, no augmentation, two or more seeds),
and every sealed test split was evaluated exactly once under a configuration
committed before the first test case was read. Where a claim rests on a
two-seed comparison the text says so; where a paired per-case statistic
exists it is reported instead of, not in addition to, an adjective.
